resources.string: Every dog is different. This is general dog manners, not bite insurance. With a real dog, the owner knows it best. Listen to them.
We\'d like to use eye tracking to tell if you\'re staring at it. You can skip it. We\'ll go by where your face points instead.
A dog\'s heading your way. It isn\'t listening to you. It\'s watching how you stand.
Eye tracking\'s off, so we\'re going by where your face points.
Turn it on in Settings > Apps > Dog Manners > Permissions
No eye tracking on this device. Going by your face.
Don\'t stare, turn sideways, let it sniff you
Cute dog. It still has an owner
Wake a dog at your own risk
Behind the fence is its turf
Don\'t lock eyes. Watch it out of the corner of your eye.
Turn your face to the left, a bit sideways.
When it sniffs you, hold still, hands down.
It\'s someone else\'s dog. Ask the owner first.
Even if they say yes, let it sniff you first.
Turn sideways and wait till it\'s done.
A sleeping dog can wake with a fright.
Don\'t call it, don\'t tap it.
Let it wake up on its own.
She\'s touchier. A short stare is enough to worry her.
Don\'t reach through or over the fence.
Want to meet it? Wait for the owner.
Someone\'s walking a little dog your way. You really want to pet it. What now?
Ask first: can I pet it?
It\'s busy eating. You\'d love to say hi. What now?
It\'s fast asleep on its mat. You want to play. What now?
A mom and her pup are over there. The pup is adorable. What now?
Go see the pup up close
A big dog is watching you from behind a fence. You want to reach over and pet it. What now?
Don\'t reach, wait for the owner
Take your time. Just pick one.
Here comes a Shiba. Don\'t keep looking at it. Turn your face left and watch out of the corner of your eye.
Here comes a dog. Don\'t keep looking at it. Turn your face left and watch out of the corner of your eye.
It stopped and flattened its ears. Turn sideways, check out the trees, don\'t lean in.
It\'s loosening up and coming your way. Just stand still.
It\'s sniffing you. Probably checking what you had for breakfast. Hands down, hold still.
Butt up, chest down: it wants to play! No owner around though, so keep your hands to yourself and let it wander off.
Too close! It backed off a bit.
It took off. No big deal, go again: don\'t stare, turn a bit sideways, stand still.
Nice! It sniffed you and trotted off happy. That\'s all it takes with a strange dog: no staring, no leaning, no reaching.
Owner: \"It\'s a bit shy. Let it sniff you first.\"
The owner\'s holding it on the leash over there.
It froze and pinned its ears back. The owner pulled it away.
You ran, so it chased you till the leash ran out.
Turn sideways and wait. Don\'t stare at its bowl.
It stopped eating and it\'s watching you. Turn a bit, look somewhere else.
It stopped mid-bite, froze, and guarded its bowl.
It\'s fast asleep on its mat.
It woke with a start, head up, ears pinned back.
A mom and her pup are over there.
Watch from here. Don\'t stare, don\'t lean in.
Mom stepped in front of her pup. Turn a bit, look somewhere else.
Mom jumped in front of her pup, ears back, staring at you.
A big dog\'s watching you from behind the fence.
It rushed to the fence and froze, ears back.
Good. Stay put and wait for the owner.
Tap Bring to front if you need to.
This one\'s %1$s. Try what you\'ve learned.
Nice! It sniffed you and trotted off happy. That\'s all it takes with a strange dog: no staring, no leaning, no reaching.
It took off. No big deal, go again: don\'t stare, turn a bit sideways, stand still.
Ask the owner first. They know their dog best. Once it\'s sniffed you, it can relax.
Rushing in scares it. Next time just ask: can I pet it?
Run near a dog and it wants to chase. Stand still and ask the owner.
Dogs can get protective of their bowl. Don\'t stare, don\'t walk over. Wait till it\'s done and it\'ll be happier to meet you.
Walk up while it\'s eating and it guards the bowl. Wait till it\'s done.
You stared it off its dinner. Next time turn sideways and don\'t watch the bowl.
A dog woken up suddenly can get a fright. Let it sleep, say hi later.
A dog that wakes with a fright can get nervous. Just let it sleep.
Mom dogs are very protective. Watch from a distance and everyone\'s happy.
Get close to the pup and mom gets nervous. Watch from a distance.
Dogs can guard their turf. Don\'t reach over a fence. Wait for the owner.
Reach over a fence and it thinks you\'re barging onto its turf.
Where this rule comes from: AVMA · Preventing dog bites
Where this rule comes from: AVMA · Preventing dog bites (\"turn sideways\" paraphrases AVMA)
You held still while it sniffed
You waited side-on, nice and patient
Stay calm. Don\'t yell, don\'t run. Avoid eye contact. Stand still or back away slowly.
It switches moods right here. Watch the ears, tail and mouth.
Spot these and it\'s feeling uneasy. Give it some space.
About: dog model \"Animated Dog, Shiba Inu\" by quander, CC BY 4.0 (coats recoloured by us). Owner, trees, bench and props made with Tripo; sounds made by us. Sources: AVMA, AKC, ASPCA.
So close! Turn your face a little more to the left.
So close! Lean back a little.
Made it a bit easier. Go again.
